note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Road Traffic Authority (RTA)'s own pages. Driver Licensing (its summary of the Road Traffic Rules - Licensing of Drivers 2017): from 1 June 2018 the RTA is responsible for driver licensing and its fees (service is delivered for it by Motor Vehicles Insurance Limited and some provincial governments); a learner's permit for a Class 1 vehicle from 18; a provisional licence after at least 3 months on the permit and the practical test, valid 12 months; a full licence to someone who has held a provisional licence (or an equivalent foreign one) for the last 12 months, so the full licence is held from 19 (18, the 3 months and the provisional year: a reading built from the Rules' stages). A full licence may be issued for 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 years at the holder's choice, so no single term is held (null). Schedule of Fees from 1 June 2018 (Road Traffic (Fees and Charges) Regulation 2017, Schedule 1, item 3): issue or renewal of a full licence K70 for one year, K130 for two, K180 for three, K230 for four, K280 for five; the fee turns on the chosen term and isn't a fixed sum by the year, so it isn't held (null). A current foreign licence is accepted in place of a PNG one rather than exchanged, so no exchange list is held.

sources.title: Driver Licensing (Road Traffic Authority, Papua New Guinea)
sources.said: RTA has overall responsibility for driver licensing and all fees and charges for driver licensing belong to, and must be remitted to, the RTA. ... This service delivery is being carried out by Motor Vehicles Insurance Limited (MVIL) and some Provincial Governments. ... 18 years of age to learn to drive a Class 1 motor vehicle or a Class 5 motor vehicle ... held a learner’s permit for the class or classes of motor vehicle for which the person is applying for a provisional driver’s licence, for a period of at least 3 months; and ... previously held, for the last 12 months- ... a provisional driver’s licence for the class or classes applied for; or ... A full drivers licence may be issued for a period of 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 years, and is valid for that period unless sooner cancelled or suspended.
